label: digit 3 input early in the original sequence (positions 0-4)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 3 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions 0-4. Every activation has in_tok == 3. It is strongest (near max) when 3 is the first occurrence at t=0-2, and weaker at t=3-4 (lower mass share). It fires only weakly and rarely at t=5 and never at t>=6. Repeat occurrences of 3 get much weaker activation (e.g. 0.3 of max), especially when an earlier 3 is already in the prefix. It does not fire on any other token, on <DEL>, or during the copy phase, even when 3 is fed back or output (fewer than 300 tiny copy-phase activations). Dev F1 0.979, precision 1.0, mass recall 0.998.

issues: The label and predicate hold up. On the test split the predicate gets precision 1.0, recall 0.961, F1 0.980 and mass recall 0.998. It has zero false positives, so every 3 input at t<=4 in the original phase fires.

The misses (3212 test steps, 0.2% of activation mass) are almost all 3 inputs at t=5 with tiny activations (0.01-0.05 of max). That is the weak tail the explanation already describes, not a systematic gap. Adding t=5 to the predicate lowers test F1 to 0.952 (precision 0.91), so t<=4 is the right cutoff.
Phase claims are confirmed. There are no activations on <DEL> and only 298 dev copy-phase activations. Every activation has in_tok == 3.

REFUTED: 'Repeat occurrences of 3 activate much more weakly (about 0.3 of max)'. This mixes up repetition with position. At a fixed t, mean activation per step (mass_recall / n_predicted, dev split) is the same for the first 3 and for repeat 3s: t=1 1.59e-5 vs 1.62e-5, t=2 1.46e-5 vs 1.47e-5, t=3 1.00e-5 vs 1.02e-5, t=4 4.6e-6 vs 4.8e-6. The top examples show this directly: 'i [3:1.00] [3:0.89] h' (a repeat at t=2 gives 0.89), '[3:0.92] s [3:0.90]' and 'k [3:0.97] p [3:0.63]'. Repeats only look weak because they tend to sit at later positions. A first 3 at t=4 is also about 0.29 ('2 p y e [3:0.29]').

The real magnitude pattern is a decay with position alone: near max at t=0-2, lower at t=3, about 0.3 at t=4, about 0.02-0.05 at t=5, and zero from t=6 on. Whether this 3 is the first 3 in the sequence has no effect.
skeptic.revised_label: digit 3 input at early original positions (0-4); strength decays with position, regardless of whether the 3 is a repeat
